counterfactual_missing_items: hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles with a greenish-black hue, especially accentuated along the dermatoglyphic ridges
a dilated eccrine duct containing amorphous pink material
decisive_items: Punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with pityriasis rosea
multiple dusky, thin plaques with a central collarette of scale
pruritic eruption that began on the trunk and gradually spread to all extremities
response.rationale: R2 is directly supported by chest and thigh biopsies consistent with pityriasis rosea and by the characteristic collarette-of-scale plaques. R1 is contradicted by the palm biopsy showing intraepidermal spongiosis and a dilated eccrine duct rather than a subepidermal blister, and by the PR-confirming biopsies. R3 is only background history and does not explain the skin eruption.

rejected.why: Palm/sole vesicles and dilated eccrine duct are not consistent with porphyria cutanea tarda; chest and thigh biopsies confirm pityriasis rosea.
Alcoholic cirrhosis is a historical comorbidity, not the diagnosis of the presenting skin eruption.
